route: Existing muted original-mission harness, copied profiles, 1400m visibility, ordinary brightness; matched render-camera gameplay checks, not mission completion or player-input responsiveness.
receiverContract: Exact existing stock/catalog identity plus opaque-world PBR/captured-lighting gate; both ambient and material records require the same valid fragment. Terrain/signpost/mixed atlas/unsupported modes retain fallback.
primarySamples: Unchanged one sample per eligible half-resolution receiver; one surface bounce, 25m transport, 45m receivers, 80m visibility. No gain or sky/reflectance/composition changes.

loaderNote: Startup also reports pre-existing external overlay-manifest and intentionally disabled implicit-layer diagnostics. These are distinct from Vulkan validation; all gameplay qualification requires validation and synchronization validation actually enabled.
limitations: 22 exact identities can receive only with reliable PBR/captured lighting and opaque coverage; no broad texture heuristics or terrain receivers.
Rock and additional wall identities are policy-enabled; this live milestone specifically demonstrates roof tiles, barn facade/door and wood, plus existing stone/concrete catalog walls.
Some original wood/plaster sections use unsupported lighting/coverage modes and intentionally remain legacy.
Unmeasured bounded stock reflectance retains baked shading; sky calibration is engine-relative.
One surface bounce, finite scene/25m transport/45m receivers/80m visibility, no indirect specular or reflected local-light illumination.
Thin/depth-discontinuous receivers can retain legacy ambient when reconstruction fails.
Existing foliage-card artifacts, texture blur, temporal/spatial noise and legacy/PBR lighting boundaries remain.
Motion checks are real render-camera mission sweeps, not player-input responsiveness or mission completion.
Screenshot ROI means are after AA/output, not raw HDR calibration. Bounce isolation is On minus sky-only, combining sunlight and reflected skylight.
Driver-free tests deliberately inject validation errors; actual gameplay logs determine zero-error Vulkan qualification.
